deviations: Zero cities founded after the pivot in 8/8 games vs the hyperwide thesis of 5-6 cities — the entire wide-flood payoff (compounding pop/science curve) was never realized.
Post-pivot unit counts (80-100 by t=160 in 5 of 8 games) are 10-12x the expected 5-8 signature; scalar growth after t=20 is almost entirely unit count, not cities or pop.
Techs flatline at 8 from t=20 in every game (the doctrine's 8-entry research lists are exhausted), so there is no 'steepest tech curve' — science contribution froze for ~140 turns.
Pop plateaus early (11-18 by t=50-60, then static), contradicting the thesis of steep population compounding.
The t=30 pivot arrives exactly when the wide thesis's own window (5-6 cities by turn 30) has closed; no check on founding space or settler safety preceded the switch.
evidence: Pivot fired in all 8 games at exactly turn 30 with cities already at 2 since t=10, satisfying both trigger conditions (turn_gte 30, own_cities_gte 2); exactly one switch per game, no flip-flops.
turtler phase honored max_cities 2: cities hold at 2 through t=30 in every game while pop grows to 11-18 and gold accumulates (e.g., s947381-r3: 106 gold at t=20).
hyperwide_flood's expected_signature ('cities 2->3 by ~10 then 5-6 by ~30') never materialized: cities remain 2 from t=10 through t=160 in all 8 games — 130 post-pivot turns produced zero new cities.

Units diverge hard from the 'stuck around 5-8' signature: post-pivot counts climb continuously, e.g., s947381-r0 16@t30 -> 90@t160 and s300003-r1 18@t30 -> 100@t160, so production sank into a unit blob instead of settler-led expansion.
Gold sawtooth matches the ~120 purchase gate in purchase_pref: repeated peaks of ~120-190 followed by ~100-120 drops (s300003-r1: 192->102->172->82; s947381-r1: 169->69->129->189->89).

s947381-r3 shows a dead equilibrium matching the documented failure mode: units pinned at 20-22, gold oscillating 70<->150, and scalar ping-ponging 1080<->1160 from t=60 to t=160 with no expansion or growth.

pivot_assessment.notes: The switch executed mechanically per spec in all 8 games (one clean turtler->hyperwide_flood at t=30, cities>=2 already true since t<=10), but it is effectively a pure timer because the cities condition is trivially pre-satisfied. Strategically the timing is poor: hyperwide_flood's thesis targets 5-6 cities BY turn 30, so pivoting AT 30 forfeits the compounding window, and empirically the post-switch doctrine changed nothing visible (cities stayed 2; units ballooned instead of settlers converting). No flip-flopping occurred — the problem is the opposite: a single one-way switch with no re-evaluation when its thesis clearly failed.

recommended_changes: Fire the pivot much earlier (turn ~12-18) or gate it on a real signal (settler available, safe corridor confirmed) instead of turn_gte 30 — as written the switch fires precisely when the wide window it is meant to exploit has already closed.

Add a post-pivot fallback/hysteresis: if cities remain at 2 for ~20 turns after the switch (true in all 8 games), revert to turtler or re-route production; currently the bot sinks ~600 production into 60-80 extra units with zero new foundings.
Add a unit cap post-pivot (e.g., ~10-15 units, one archer/spear per city per the expected signature) so the SETTLER/GRANARY build order actually gets built instead of looping into a 90-100 unit blob.

Check expand_ring 3 feasibility before switching (or allow ring 4-5 fallback): s947381-r3's frozen units/scalar oscillation matches the documented 'founding space inside ring 3 runs out' failure mode.
Extend research lists beyond the 8 techs (every game flatlines at techs=8 from t=20) or convert surplus science to gold to fund the ~120 granary/settler purchases.
